document.title: Memo from Richard Clarke to Condoleezza Rice requesting urgent Principals-level review of the al-Qaeda network
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Bush Administration's First Memo on al-Qaeda Declassified
document.note: Clarke's memo to National Security Adviser Rice requests an immediate Principals Committee meeting on al-Qaeda. It urges covert aid to the Northern Alliance and Uzbekistan, a larger counterterrorism budget, and a decision on responding to the USS Cole attack. It carries a declassification stamp of April 7, 2004, and attached two documents: Tab A (December 2000 strategy paper) and Tab B (the 1998 Delenda Plan, still classified).

events.description: Clarke sends memo to Rice requesting an urgent Principals-level review of the al-Qida network.
Attack on the USS Cole; the response decision remains pending (the memo does not give the date; October 2000 comes from outside knowledge).
Year-end 2000 strategy paper on eliminating the threat from al-Qida's jihadist networks produced by the Clinton Administration.
September 1998 Pol-Mil Plan for al-Qida produced.
Clarke sends a memo to Rice urgently requesting a Principals Committee review of the al Qida network.
At the close of the Clinton Administration, two al Qida decisions were deferred to the Bush Administration: aid to the Northern Alliance and aid to Uzbekistan.
The Clinton Administration developed a year-end 2000 strategy on al Qida.
A September 1998 Pol-Mil Plan for al-Qida was produced.
Attack on the USS Cole, to which the new Administration must decide how to respond.
Fighting is expected to resume in spring after the winter thaw, with the Northern Alliance at risk of being taken out of action.

September 1998 Paper: Pol-Mil Plan for al-Qida (Tab B)
key_claims: Clarke argues al-Qida is a major transnational threat that should not be handled as a narrow terrorist issue within regional policies.
Al-Qida seeks to drive the US out of the Muslim world and replace moderate regimes with Taliban-style theocracies.
The memo says al-Qida's 55 Brigade is a key Taliban fighting force and could be freed to threaten US interests elsewhere if the Northern Alliance collapses in the spring.
Two decisions deferred by the Clinton Administration concern aid to the Northern Alliance and aid to Uzbekistan against the al-Qida/IMU threat.
Clarke proposes early, strong messages to the Taliban and Pakistan about ending the al-Qida sanctuary in Afghanistan.
Efforts to go after al-Qida's money and counter its propaganda have not worked effectively.
Clarke advises responding to the USS Cole attack at a time and manner of US choosing rather than with knee-jerk reactions.
